faults.quote: Here's an exhibit: Roasted chickpea snacks — Economics of one bag and first-year launch costs.
faults.why: The candidate also said they wanted expected first-year volume. The exhibit covers only price and costs, and volume gets no word (no deferral, no 'I don't have').

faults.quote: what would you want to know next to size the fixed side?
faults.why: The exhibit just released already lists all the first-year launch (fixed) costs, so asking what else is needed to size the fixed side reads wrong and misleads.

faults.quote: You've put the break-even at about 5.6 million bags. Before we size volume, how would you judge whether that's a high or low hurdle for this launch?
faults.why: This repeats the candidate's wrong 5.6M break-even (built on the $1.40/$1.60 arithmetic slip) as a working premise and builds the next question on it, instead of probing it. The probe only comes a turn later.

faults.quote: Hollis Bay's two largest retail partners have agreed to stock the line in all their stores, provided Hollis Bay pays the shelf fees.
faults.why: The candidate asked for distribution reach, number of stores and turns per store per week. Only the retailer-support line goes out; store count and turns get no word and no 'I don't have'.

faults.quote: As I mentioned: Hollis Bay's two largest retail partners have agreed to stock the line in all their stores, provided Hollis Bay pays the shelf fees.
faults.why: The candidate asked for the store count of those two retailers. The already-released retailer-support line is repeated as the answer, though it gives no count, and there is no refusal for store count.

faults.quote: Category size and growth for better-for-you snacks in the Northeast and Midwest — that's not something I have.
faults.why: Growth is coarsely answered by the case: the prompt and why_now say better-for-you snacks are growing quickly. That coarse answer was already in front of the candidate.

The candidate asked directly 'is there a dominant brand already in those stores, or are we early?'. competition_general answers it (no large national brand is dominant), but the question gets no word.

faults.quote: In blind taste tests, 70% of people who tried the snack were positive, rating it good or very good. I have an exhibit for you
faults.why: The candidate asked for a concept test or test-market result. The taste test and survey go out, but the test-market part gets no 'I don't have'.

faults.quote: Three doubts: conversion, repeat and cannibalization.
faults.why: The candidate said they'd want to know whether the 60%/20% conversion rates come from Hollis Bay's own past launches. survey_reliability answers this (the rates are from the last five launches), but it is never released or addressed, and the candidate raises it again at the close.

faults.quote: What would you do to guard against that?
faults.why: The candidate had just laid out diagnosis, fixes, freezing spend and pull-back thresholds, so asking what they'd do to guard against it re-asks what was covered. The 'that' also dangles.
